findings.reason: the four deliverables need four measures and four controls; as one node it will be built and closed on the weakest of them, and the obligations and reroute requirements are already the substance of other sections.
findings.text: §24's Deliverable states four separate requirements — a queued run's recorded backend is the launchable lane; a review composed with no lane named never resolves to an excluded backend; a queued pointer whose backend no admission service drains is refused or rerouted; and a queued run past its review-queued bound raises a duty — so the node cannot be reviewed or closed on one verdict and its single gate proves none of them fully

findings.reason: a done-when whose controls do not cover two of its measured behaviours cannot show those guards fire, so those halves pass however the code behaves.
findings.text: the single negative control ("with the queued backend left as the metered one, `admit_once` for the local lane launches nothing") exercises only the backend-rewrite assertion, so the "backend no service drains is refused or rerouted" assertion and the "obligations view reports a review-queued run past its bound" assertion are asserted without any control that could falsify them

findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching §24 on its declared scope cannot satisfy an assertion that lives in a module the node does not own; the dependency on §5 (or the obligations write path) must be declared or the assertion dropped.
findings.text: §24's done-when requires "the obligations view reports a review-queued run past its bound for the session that queued it", but §24 has `data-links=""` and its write paths are `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `dispatch_plan.py`, `queue_admission.py`, `recovery_review_dispatch.py` and the new test — `reckon/crew/obligations.py` is not among them, and §5 already owns the obligations reading ("beside its existing `review-queued` reading, whose 30-minute bound is unchanged")

findings.reason: the deliverable asserts a fix ("never resolves to a backend in `review_excluded_backends`") on a cause the plan has not shown ran, so the node would aim its repair at a path that may never have been taken; the plan should locate the caller or narrow the deliverable to "find and report the site".
findings.text: the Why names a second fault, "a review composed with no lane named resolved to `codex`, although `review_excluded_backends` is meant to keep reviews off metered lanes", but the same paragraph states "the site where `local` and the resolved backend part company is not yet known", and the cited evidence points away from that mechanism: the pointer recorded `local: true`, and a review with `local` set is routed through `flight.select_local_backend` in `_dispatch_composed_review` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1804-1810`), while the excluded-backend consult lives in `_ordered_review_lanes` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1186`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited discard json, `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` and `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py` all resolve; there are no extensionless hrefs in §24.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §24 declares one negative control, which falsifies only the backend-rewrite assertion; the refuse-or-reroute assertion and the obligations-duty assertion are measured with no control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §24's gate logs go "under the run directory" and its cited discard record is on the operator's durable config path, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §24 names no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags; the new file `test_a_queued_run_waits_on_its_lane.py` is mechanism-named.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §24's second fault asserts the review "resolved to codex, although `review_excluded_backends` is meant to keep reviews off metered lanes", yet the plan concedes the site is unknown and cites no evidence the compose path that ran ever consults that exclusion.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §24 carries four independent deliverables (queue the launchable backend, honour `review_excluded_backends` at compose, refuse-or-reroute an undrained pointer, raise an obligations duty).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §24 declares no relationship (empty `data-links`) to §5, although its done-when measures the obligations view §5 owns.
